items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: when we had to play the big shows with Troy S. Ben

ctx.x: In listening to their recordings, you know, of the Shadowland and Dreamland blues, I had to hear things, it sounds like they're doing a lot of playing by ear. They are. On those particular recordings.

There weren't any written arrangements as far as that's concerned, unless it was what we call stock arrangements. And everybody didn't read? No. In fact when they were playing, when we had to play the big shows with Troy S. Ben, I had to use the piano part, the violin part, the trumpet part, and the clarinet part. And Pete jumped from one to the other to fit in to make the music right for the performance we were playing for. Could you transpose it? Sure, I can transpose it aside. I can transpose it from a violin…
You learn something new every day.
